original_test_intent: Validate the vendor-defined platform-management I3C path associated with CPU1 by confirming the approved controller and expected targets/addresses and collecting bounded response and health evidence.
original_method: After the project supplies and approves the CPU1 BMC/OOB controller, bus, target identity/address lifecycle, vendor-supported tool and expected responses, collect complete baseline state and run only the defined non-mutating discovery or read operation.
manual_activity: The CPU/platform owner supplies the CPU1 management-I3C package, validates target ownership and dynamic-address behavior, approves one bounded read method and interprets the final evidence.
required_inputs: BMC/OOB controller and authenticated access path
Expected target PID/BCR/DCR and static/dynamic address map
Vendor-supported non-mutating tool and exact transaction
CPU1 thermal/power/BMC health limits, aborts and recovery
safety_requirements: Never reuse the same-code PCIe Connector procedure or evidence
Do not treat Linux sysfs as proof of the BMC CPU1 target
Do not assume i2c-tools or i3cdetect is safe for this platform
Do not initiate DAA, CCC, reset or writes without explicit approval
Protect credentials and verified host identity
Capture complete output rather than tail fragments
Stop on address reassignment, target loss, bus lock, thermal/power or BMC anomaly
agent_execution_scope: Keep row 1816 bound to variant f8b4026eb34a77ea
Reject cross-variant PCIe and host-only I3C evidence
Validate the supplied management topology and tool contract
After approval, collect only the exact bounded read and complete health evidence
Perform no DAA, CCC, write, reset or recovery on its own
Report evidence without a formal verdict
engineer_actions: Bind CPU1 to the exact management controller, bus and targets
Approve address lifecycle, supported tool and read operation
Define expected responses and health thresholds
Review evidence and issue the verdict

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Not sufficient. Host sysfs and selected dmesg tails cannot prove the Wistron BMC/platform-management CPU1 route, and the proposed i3cdetect behavior is not defined for the target/address lifecycle.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use only the project-approved BMC/OOB vendor command after the controller, target set, address semantics and expected responses are bound; capture its complete raw output and correlated platform health.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: CPU1 and the two-minute planning fields are preserved. No bus number, dynamic address, target, tool syntax or expected value is inferred.

modernized_recommendation.status: REQUIRES CPU1 I3C PACKAGE AND CONFIRMATION
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Record immutable CPU1/BMC/platform identity, capture controller and target state through the documented management path, perform one approved non-mutating vendor read, and compare full topology, responses and CPU1 thermal/power/BMC health before and after.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Supplies the absent execution contract without rewriting the Master placeholders and removes generic host enumeration as acceptance evidence.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Host kernel visibility alone does not cover BMC route ownership, CPU1 association, target identity, address lifecycle or expected response.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Dynamic discovery or CCCs may reassign addresses or disturb CPU1-attached thermal, power, sensor or management targets.

project_override_considerations: The explicit row-1816 ruling fixes the capability class at REQUIRES while inputs are pending. A project may bind a platform-specific BMC route and tool, but cannot substitute row-16 PCIe handling or generic host sysfs for CPU1 I3C coverage.
expected_evidence: Exact source key, variant and duplicate-code separation
Approved CPU1 I3C package, owner and timestamp
BMC/OOB controller, bus and CPU1 association
Target PID/BCR/DCR and static/dynamic address lifecycle
Exact tool/version/transaction and complete raw output
CPU1 thermal/power, BMC SEL/SDR and platform-health evidence

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The row's item and placeholders do not contradict each other. Reuse of the code by a PCIe Connector row is a source-identity collision handled by sheet, physical row, variant and hash; it does not merge or invalidate this row's I3C intent.

blocked_analysis.analysis: CPU1 I3C purpose, management target class, bounded read operation, safety boundary and evidence can be specified. Missing project controller, address, vendor-tool and expected-response values prevent execution now but are not an irreducible blocker under ED-04 and the explicit row-1816 ruling.

review_improvement: Preserves the approved REQUIRES classification, explicitly separates the same-code PCIe variant, and strengthens the plan from generic host enumeration to a project-bound BMC/OOB controller, target and address-lifecycle contract.
independent_technical_reasoning: This row differs from the same-code PCIe row in every operative identity field and must never inherit its physical procedure. CPU1 I3C discovery can alter dynamic addressing, so no generic scan is safe or conclusive. However, the owner can bind the BMC controller, target identities, allowed read and acceptance oracle without changing the Master intent; that makes automation conditional on a package and confirmation rather than impossible.
